title: Design: AI chat service
objective: Design a chat service that calls a language model: limits, conversation history, streaming replies, and failure handling.

sources.title: Claude Platform docs: Streaming messages (server-sent events)
Claude Platform docs: Context windows (the history sent with each turn has a limit)
Claude Platform docs: Rate limits (429 responses)

simplifies: One model provider and one region. Real services also add safety filtering, prompt caching, usage billing, monitoring of quality and cost, and fallbacks to other models.

steps.caption: A user sends a message. The gateway checks who they are and applies a per-user rate limit: every model call costs money.
The chat service loads the conversation history. The model only knows what is sent with each request, and that has a size limit (the context window), so long chats are trimmed or summarised.

predict.prompt: The model remembers nothing between requests. How does it know what was said earlier?

options.text: The service sends the relevant history with every request
options.explanation: Right. The history travels with each request, within the context window's limit.

options.text: The model stores every chat itself
options.explanation: Each request stands alone; the service supplies the history.
Without the history, it can't follow the conversation.

steps.caption: The service calls the model API with streaming on, so text arrives piece by piece (server-sent events) instead of all at the end.

predict.prompt: A full reply takes 10 seconds to generate. Why stream it?

options.text: The user sees words appear within moments, instead of waiting 10 seconds for nothing
options.explanation: Right. The total time is similar, but the wait feels far shorter.

options.text: Streaming makes the model generate faster
options.explanation: Generation speed is the same; only delivery changes.
Cost depends on tokens, not on streaming.

steps.caption: The service relays the stream to the app as it arrives.
When the reply is complete, it is saved to history with a message id, so a retried request can't save it twice.
Failures: the model API can answer 429 (rate limited) or be slow. Retry with backoff, set a timeout, and show a clear message rather than spinning forever.

predict.prompt: The model API returns 429 Too Many Requests. What should the chat service do?

options.text: Wait, then retry with backoff, and tell the user if it still can't
options.explanation: Right. Retrying instantly in a loop makes the overload worse.
That hammers a service that has asked you to slow down.
The user deserves a clear message instead of silence.

quiz.prompt: Why is a per-user rate limit especially important for an AI chat service?

options.text: Each request costs real money and capacity, so one user (or a bug) could run up huge costs
options.explanation: Right. Limits protect both the budget and other users.

options.text: Models can only answer one user at a time
options.explanation: They serve many at once; the limit is about cost and fairness.

quiz.prompt: A conversation has grown past the model's context window. What does the service do?

options.text: Trim or summarise older history so the request fits
options.explanation: Right. Only what fits in the window can be sent.
The request would be rejected or cut off.

options.text: Start a new conversation without telling the user
options.explanation: Silently losing context surprises users; trimming or summarising keeps the gist.
